assign.brief: Owner's question on /framework/ux/Dictate/ (2026-10-01), about the ✦ Ask by voice full-height mobile sheet: on an ordinary page, scrolling down makes Chrome's own address bar/toolbar auto-hide, and scrolling up a little brings it back. The owner wants to know if that can happen on this full-screen sheet too, and suspects the reason it doesn't is that the chat thread scrolls in its OWN nested scroll area (a sub-scroll div) rather than the page itself scrolling — Chrome's chrome-hide behavior only responds to the page's own scroll, not a nested scrollable element. Owner's own words: 'maybe we draw out the whole chat without its own sub-scroll area so that the whole page is bigger and then we scroll the whole page to the bottom, rather than having a nested scroll area... I'm not sure the best way to handle that, I'm not sure what kind of layout we're using, I'm not sure how this thing is being positioned, so there's a lot of questions there.' Investigate: find the sheet's current layout/scroll structure (ext/drawer/, ext/Chat), confirm whether it's a nested scroll area, and research/prototype whether switching to page-level scroll (while still keeping the composer/bottom bar pinned, and the sticky-bottom auto-scroll behavior from the chat-autoscroll task) would let Chrome's native toolbar-hide kick in on mobile — or whether a fixed-position sheet (likely position:fixed, which breaks document scroll) is what's actually blocking it, in which case say so clearly as the real constraint. Report findings; only change code if a clean fix is found and verified on a real phone-width headless shot. Land per finish-task either way (a 'here's why it can't/can' answer is a valid landing).

log.msg: Read ext/drawer/readme.md, doc/sheet.md and doc/decisions.md, then rail.js + rail.css + Widget.css + Page.css + framework.css. Confirmed the sheet's own scroll structure: .drawer-rail-sheet is position: fixed; inset-inline: 0; inset-block-end: 0, even in its 'full' state (rail.css lines 74-110) — a box stacked over the real page, not part of it. Inside it, the thread that actually scrolls (.drawer-rail-sheet-thread, overflow-y: auto, rail.css line 177; or Widget.js's own .ux-dictate-widget-thread / -feed-wrap, Widget.css lines 20-21 and 162-165) is a second, separate overflow box, wrapped by the head row and the composer as flex siblings, not the whole fixed box.

Checked whether an ordinary page on this site even scrolls the document itself, since the owner's fix idea depends on that. It does not: framework.css pins html, body and .app to exactly 100% height (lines 370-428), so the real <body> never scrolls on any page here. .pages (core/Page/Page.css line 58-63) is overflow-y: scroll and is the one box every ordinary page actually scrolls — confirmed by ext/Inbox's own css comment calling .pages out by name as the page's one scrollbar.

decision.what: The real blocker is not 'a nested scroll area' by itself — it is two separate facts. (1) Chromium promotes whichever single scrollable box fills almost the whole viewport, with nothing competing, to drive the toolbar auto-hide (its 'implicit root scroller' heuristic) — .pages already is that box on every ordinary page, and it is itself a nested overflow div, not the literal document, yet the toolbar already hides on it. So nested scroll alone was never disqualifying. (2) The sheet fails for two independent reasons instead: position:fixed stacks it OVER .pages rather than inside it, so the box Chrome already promoted (.pages) sits underneath, covered, never moving while the sheet is scrolled — and even on its own terms the sheet's own thread never fills the whole screen by itself, since the head row and composer are separate flex siblings around it, so it could never qualify for promotion either.
decision.alternative_considered: Just removing the inner overflow:auto on the thread and calling that 'page-level scroll' — rejected as insufficient on its own: the page underneath (.pages) is itself a nested div sitting beneath the fixed sheet and unreachable by it, so position:fixed has to go too, which is the real surgery, not a one-line change.

log.msg: Worked out the shape of a real fix, for the record: make the thread itself the one position:fixed; inset:0 box while the sheet is full, with the head and the composer laid out as position:sticky children INSIDE that same scrolling box instead of flex siblings around it, and hide .pages outright (display:none, not just a lower z-index) while full, so it stops being the box Chrome already promoted. This reaches the grip handle's height math, the composer's keyboard-avoidance, and the sticky-bottom autoscroll from ext/Chat/doc/scroll.md (the chat-autoscroll task, same day) — all three currently assume today's head/composer-as-siblings shape.

decision.what: Did not build the restructure described above.
decision.why: There is no way to verify the one thing that actually matters here — whether Chrome's real address bar hides — without a real Android phone running real Chrome. A headless screenshot (Playwright, the site MCP's shot tool, devtools device emulation) never draws Chrome's own browser chrome at all; the 'device' in every one of those tools IS the whole viewport, so no screenshot, however carefully set up, could ever show this behavior working or not. Landing a real rewrite of a part of the sheet that had three separate regressions land the same day (fullscreen-rail-void, voice-sheet-header) with no way to confirm the fix does the one thing it exists for is the wrong trade.
decision.alternative: Could have built it speculatively and shipped unverified — rejected: real regression risk on fragile, just-stabilized code, for a change whose entire purpose cannot be checked with any tool available here. Documented the exact recipe in doc/sheet.md instead, as the scoped follow-up task if the owner still wants it and can test it on an actual phone.
